key_insight: Extending many-hypercube concatenated quantum codes from qubits to prime-dimensional qudits improves error-correction performance, with higher local dimension q yielding markedly better thresholds and a strong waterfall regime.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest qudit-based FTQC architectures can achieve higher-rate protection with better decoding performance than qubit-only designs, especially as local dimension increases.
method: Generalized level-2 and level-3 many-hypercube (MHC) codes to prime-dimensional qudits.
Extended the level-by-level minimum-distance (LLMD) decoder to the qudit setting.
Analyzed performance under a qudit X-error model using code-capacity simulations and entropy-based decoder interpretation.
evidence_signal: In code-capacity evaluations up to q=13, the threshold rose monotonically from 5.1% for qubits to 10.0% for q=13, with stronger-than-expected logical suppression in the high-q waterfall regime.
watch_item: The reported gains are shown for an X-error model and code-capacity setting, so performance under more realistic noise, other error types, and hardware constraints still needs verification.
paper_title: High-Rate Concatenated Quantum Error-Correcting Codes for Qudits
